# Write the JSON object below to $CODEX_HOME/hooks.json ($CODEX_HOME defaults
# to ~/.codex). Then start `codex`, and at its "Hooks need review" prompt
# choose "Trust all and continue". Until you do, every hook is skipped —
# see the warning further down. Outside roost these hooks are silent no-ops.
#
# Copy the object, NOT these comment lines: hooks.json is strict JSON and has
# no comment syntax.
#
# | codex hook          | state                                |
# |---------------------|--------------------------------------|
# | UserPromptSubmit    | working                              |
# | PostToolUse         | working (and it is what clears 🛑)    |
# | PermissionRequest   | blocked                              |
# | Stop                | done, plus the turn's reply          |
# | Stop, with no reply | error                                |
# | Interrupt           | idle (clears 🛑 after No or Esc)      |
#
# PostToolUse is what clears 🛑 after "Yes". No hook fires when you answer a
# permission dialog, so it is the first observable event afterwards — measured
# on codex-cli 0.151.0, one second after "1. Yes, proceed". After "No", or Esc,
# the tool never runs and Interrupt is what fires instead — measured on
# codex-cli 0.154.0, within 100ms, with no Stop after it.
#
# Interrupt was added in a later roost release than the other four. If you
# trusted roost's hooks before it was there, codex asks at "Hooks need review"
# again for that one handler: answer "Trust all and continue" once more. Until
# you do, a declined dialog leaves 🛑 stamped, and `roost doctor` says so.
#
# Interrupt asks for 3 seconds where the other four ask for 10, and that is
# codex's own cap, not a roost preference: codex clamps an Interrupt hook to 3s
# and used to print `warning: clamping Interrupt hook timeout to 3s` — naming
# this file's full path — on every start. The hook always ran with 3 seconds;
# only the warning has gone. If you trusted a roost hooks.json that still said
# 10, codex asks at "Hooks need review" once more for Interrupt alone, because
# the number it hashed has moved. Answer "Trust all and continue"; until you
# do, a declined dialog leaves 🛑 stamped, and `roost doctor` says so.
#
# There is no error EVENT. Codex has twelve hook events and none of them reports
# an error, so 💥 is inferred: a Stop that carries no reply means the turn most
# likely never reached the model. Some dead turns still end ✅ done. See
# docs/known-gaps.md, which lists which ones, and the Codex section of
# site/content/docs/state-badges.md, which says it to users.
#
# THESE HANDLER OBJECTS ARE FROZEN, and that is not a style note. Codex
# stores a hash of each normalised handler in $CODEX_HOME/config.toml and
# SKIPS any handler whose hash no longer matches — with nothing printed on
# stdout, on stderr, or in the TUI. Measured on codex-cli 0.150.1: appending one
# argument to a command string took 8 of 8 hooks down, and changing a single
# timeout from 10 to 11 took 7 of 8 down. So editing a command or a timeout in a
# later roost release would silently un-badge every machine that had already
# granted trust. Everything roost might want to change later lives inside
# adapters/codex/roost-codex-hook instead, which codex re-reads on every run and
# never hashes. Adding a NEW event to this file is safe (measured on 0.151.0:
# the handlers already trusted kept firing); editing one that is already here is
# not.
#
# Interrupt's timeout is the single exception ever made, and it cleared a bar
# no other edit has: codex was already clamping that number, so the edit cost
# one re-trust and changed nothing the hook does. An edit that also changed
# behaviour would trade a working badge on every trusted machine for the fix,
# and does not clear it.
#
# The trust prompt vouches for a PATH, not for the code at that path. Anyone who
# can write adapters/codex/roost-codex-hook changes what runs, with no second
# review. That is codex's model, not something roost adds.
{
  "hooks": {
    "UserPromptSubmit": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "@@ROOST_HOME@@/adapters/codex/roost-codex-hook UserPromptSubmit", "timeout": 10 } ] }
    ],
    "PostToolUse": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "@@ROOST_HOME@@/adapters/codex/roost-codex-hook PostToolUse", "timeout": 10 } ] }
    ],
    "PermissionRequest": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "@@ROOST_HOME@@/adapters/codex/roost-codex-hook PermissionRequest", "timeout": 10 } ] }
    ],
    "Stop": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "@@ROOST_HOME@@/adapters/codex/roost-codex-hook Stop", "timeout": 10 } ] }
    ],
    "Interrupt": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "@@ROOST_HOME@@/adapters/codex/roost-codex-hook Interrupt", "timeout": 3 } ] }
    ]
  }
}
